questions.q: Why does the pip-audit workflow step use continue-on-error: true?
options: Because pip-audit cannot produce JSON output otherwise
Because GitHub Actions requires every step to continue regardless of outcome
To skip the dependency scan entirely on pull requests
So pip-audit's own exit code doesn't abort the job before the gate script can apply its own severity threshold
questions.explain: pip-audit exits non-zero on any finding, including Low severity ones. continue-on-error lets the scan finish and produce a report so the gate script, not the scanner's raw exit code, makes the actual pass/fail call.

questions.q: Why does security_gate.py read both the pip-audit and bandit JSON reports itself, instead of trusting each tool's own exit code?
options: JSON parsing is required by GitHub Actions for all workflow steps
So one consistent severity threshold is applied in one place, instead of maintaining two different failure rules across two tools
Because bandit and pip-audit cannot both run in the same job
Because exit codes are not supported in Ubuntu runners
questions.explain: Trusting each scanner's own exit code would mean two separate, possibly inconsistent thresholds. One gate script reading both reports makes a single deliberate decision.

questions.q: Why does count_blocking_findings() only count Critical and High severity findings as build-blocking?
options: Low and Medium findings are not real security issues
Because bandit cannot report severities below High
Failing the build on every Low/Medium finding trains developers to ignore the gate; blocking only on Critical/High keeps it meaningful
GitHub Actions does not support more than two severity levels
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly ties this threshold to Chapter 6's lesson on gates that don't slow every build -- blocking on everything erodes trust in the gate within days.

questions.q: Why does the artifact-upload step use if: always()?
options: So the scan reports still get attached to the run even when the security-gate step above it fails and stops the job
Because GitHub Actions deletes all artifacts by default
To force the workflow to run on every branch, not just pull requests
Because bandit requires always() to produce output
questions.explain: Without if: always(), a failed gate step would stop the job before the reports get uploaded, forcing a reviewer to re-run the scan locally just to see what failed.

questions.q: What is the real proof, described in Step 6, that the security gate actually works?
options: Confirming the workflow YAML has no syntax errors
Reading the gate script's source code carefully one time
Opening a PR with a known-vulnerable dependency pinned and watching the required check actually fail, then reverting and watching it pass again
Checking that bandit and pip-audit are both listed in requirements.txt
questions.explain: A gate that has only ever been observed passing has never really been tested -- seeing it fail on a deliberately bad input, then pass again after the fix, is what verifies it.
